findings.summary: main() ran at import time, so importing the shared user list re-seeded as a side effect and any transient failure called process.exit(1) during module load, killing the whole Playwright run with a misleading stack. Fixed by extracting the list to the side-effect-free scripts/dev-seed-user-list.ts (an import.meta guard was tried first and rejected — Playwright transpiles specs to CJS where import.meta is a syntax error).

The unauthenticated like-redirect test wrapped its only assertion in if (await isVisible().catch(() => false)), so it passed with zero assertions whenever the selector drifted or the seed emptied. Guard removed; the like button is now asserted visible unconditionally before the click.

drop policy had no if exists, so a re-run failed. Added if exists and proved idempotency by applying the file twice. Matters more than usual here because the migration was applied via psql outside CLI tracking.

The doc comment still claimed self-like was deliberately not a DB constraint, contradicting the new migration. Rewritten to state both layers enforce it and why the server action alone is insufficient (a caller with their own token can POST to /rest/v1/kudos_likes directly).

MAX_HASHTAGS/MIN_HASHTAGS are duplicated in the composer, src/lib/kudos/create-kudos.ts and the DB check constraint, and the composer's export has zero importers. Deferred deliberately: plans/260911-1143-viet-kudo-screen phase 02 creates the shared hashtag-bounds module and restructures this file, so consolidating now would be churn.

404 lines, over the project's 200-line guideline — a direct consequence of moving the six fixme tests verbatim. Deferred to phase 05, which rewrites those bodies and is the natural place to split the file. Note home.spec.ts (424) and awards-information.spec.ts (462) already exceed it, so this is a pre-existing property of e2e/.
